correctness.rationale: For every normalized three-site vector on Z5, Weyl orthogonality makes the 25 matrix-lifting singular values exactly sqrt(5) times all 25 ambiguity moduli, largest sqrt(5). Every support is affine-equivalent to 0,1,2. Delay two has modulus s=uw; delay one has five points with sharp upper bound sqrt(t(1-t-phi*s)), phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2, t=v^2. Completing the square proves mu<=min(s,(1-phi*s)/2)<=alpha=(5-sqrt(5))/10. Equality forces s=t=alpha and phase curvature a fifth root. The nondegenerate endpoint amplitude quadratic gives two unordered squares; at that solution every delay-zero squared modulus is among 1, sqrt(5)/5, and (3sqrt(5)-5)/10, all exceeding alpha^2. This proves attainment, necessity, and complete equality class. Missing delays exclude supports <=2 and consecutive triples at N>=6. The actual package CHECK.py completed 5259 numerical checks, including independent full matrix SVD; numerical checks are only corroboration.

value.rationale: Full cyclic Gabor matrix tomography is a natural informationally complete design criterion. Three sites are the least possible window support on Z5, so determining its true worst-direction stability is a canonical smallest-support design problem. The theorem gives the exact sharp global condition number, explicit all-complex optimizer classification, and strict support boundary; a full minimax classification is not a trivial injectivity consequence. It informs conditioning tradeoffs for minimal-support finite STFT sensing, without claiming broad prime-dimension generalization.
